G1 · Required and preferred job skills

repo://ai-services/knowledge/jobs/required-skills.md#chunk-1

Read the job description and listed skills together. Required skills are stated employer requirements; preferred skills are desirable rather than mandatory. Prepare examples that demonstrate each stated skill. A missing skill label does not establish a requirement. If the posting does not distinguish required and preferred skills, explain the uncertainty rather than making that distinction yourself.

G2 · Preparing evidence for a job application

repo://ai-services/knowledge/jobs/preparation.md#chunk-1

Prepare for a job application by matching the posting's stated responsibilities and skills to specific projects or work examples. Describe what you did and the result, using only achievements you can support. For an unfamiliar skill, plan a small practice project. General preparation advice is not an extra employer requirement and does not guarantee selection.

G3 · Interpreting job posting details

repo://ai-services/knowledge/jobs/posting-details.md#chunk-1

Use the selected job posting for its location, employment type, experience level, salary range, closing date and status. Missing salary values mean salary is unspecified, not zero. Do not infer currency, benefits, visa sponsorship, remote work or hiring eligibility when absent. Check unclear or outdated details with the employer before relying on them.
